newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela Mavesa seeks to expact Andean pact sales.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela Mavesa seeks to expact Andean pact sales.

text.p: Leading Venezuelan foods group Mavesa expects to invest between $20 and $80 million in the coming year as part of a move to expand sales among Andean pact countries, financial vice-president Manuel Sucre said.
"We're interested in acquisitions or associations, be that in Colombia, Peru or Ecuador, principally in foods and cleaning products," Sucre told reporters after the company's annual general meeting.
Sucre said the expansion could be easily financed, "given the company's low debt levels."
In addition, a further issue of American Depository Receipts, which currently account for 35 percent of the company, was another possibility, he added.

In fiscal 1996, exports reached $17 million, or six percent of total sales. Net profits for the year rose to 14 billion bolivars, on 139 billion bolivars of sales, compared with 9.0 billion profits on 117.3 billion of sales in the year before.
